p2.q: Describe a journey you remember well.
model: I'd like to talk about a trip I took to Hokkaido with my family two years ago. We flew from Haneda to New Chitose Airport, and it was my first time on a large plane, a Boeing seven-seven-seven. I went with my parents and my younger brother. The flight itself was only about ninety minutes, but I remember almost every minute of it. I had a window seat, and when we took off, I could see Mount Fuji above the clouds. A cabin attendant even gave me a small card about the aircraft. The main reason I remember this journey so well is that it was the moment I decided I wanted to become a pilot. Before that trip, I just thought planes were cool, but seeing the view from the cockpit window when we visited after landing made me realise it could be a real job. So, for me, it wasn't just a holiday, it was the start of my dream.

model: The skill I'd really like to learn is flying a small aircraft, like a Cessna. I think I would learn it at a flying club or a flight school, where an instructor sits next to you and explains everything step by step. Before actually flying, I would probably practise on a flight simulator, because it's much cheaper and you can make mistakes safely. I imagine it would be quite difficult. You have to control the plane, talk to air traffic control in English and keep checking the instruments, all at the same time. Landing especially seems tricky, because you have to judge the wind. The reason I want to learn this skill is that I'm hoping to become an airline pilot. Before her lessons, I was quite shy and hated speaking in front of others. Because of her, I started to enjoy English, and now it's one of my favourite subjects. ielts_p3_1a.q: What problems do commuters face in big cities?
ielts_p3_1a.ja: 大都市の通勤者はどんな問題を抱えていますか。
model: Crowded trains and long journeys are the biggest problems. Many people spend two hours a day commuting, which leaves them tired and with little free time.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: What are the benefits of tourism for a country?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 観光は国にどんな利益をもたらしますか。
model: Tourism creates jobs, especially in hotels and restaurants, and brings money into local areas. It can also help people from different countries understand each other better.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: Can tourism cause problems for local people?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 観光は地元の人々に問題を起こすことがありますか。
model: Yes, it can. In very popular places, too many visitors cause crowded streets and rising prices, so it becomes harder for local people to live there.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: Is it better to travel alone or in a group?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 一人旅とグループ旅行、どちらが良いですか。
model: It depends on the person. Travelling alone gives you more freedom and makes you talk to local people, whereas travelling in a group is safer and usually more fun.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: How might holidays change in the future?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 将来、休暇の過ごし方はどう変わるでしょうか。
model: I think people may take shorter trips closer to home to reduce their carbon footprint. Virtual reality might also let people "visit" places before they decide to go there.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: Why do people like to visit famous landmarks?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: なぜ人々は有名な名所を訪れたがるのですか。
model: Partly because they want to see with their own eyes something they have seen in pictures for years. Taking a photo there also gives people a sense of achievement.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: Should popular tourist sites limit the number of visitors?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 人気の観光地は訪問者の数を制限すべきですか。
model: In some cases, yes. If a place is too crowded, it can be damaged, and visitors cannot enjoy it either. A booking system is a fair way to manage numbers.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: How can tourists show respect for local cultures?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 観光客はどうやって地元の文化への敬意を示せますか。
model: By learning a few words of the local language and following local customs, for example dressing modestly at religious sites.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_1b.q: Do you think travel helps people understand each other?
ielts_p3_1b.ja: 旅行は人々の相互理解に役立つと思いますか。
model: Yes. Meeting people from other countries face to face breaks down stereotypes. You realise that people everywhere have similar hopes and worries.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Which skills are most useful for young people today?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: 今の若者にとっていちばん役に立つスキルは何ですか。
model: I would say communication skills and digital skills. Almost every job now involves working with computers and explaining ideas to other people, often in English.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or by yourself online?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: スキルは先生から学ぶのとオンラインで独学するのと、どちらが良いですか。
model: For practical skills, a teacher is better because they can correct your mistakes immediately. However, online courses are cheaper and flexible, so they are good for the basics.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Why do some people give up learning new skills?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: 新しいスキルの習得をあきらめてしまう人がいるのはなぜですか。
model: Often because they expect quick results. When progress becomes slow, they lose motivation, especially if they are busy with work or school.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Should schools teach more practical skills, like cooking or managing money?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: 学校は料理やお金の管理などの実用的なスキルをもっと教えるべきですか。
model: Yes, I think so. These skills are needed by everyone, and not all families have time to teach them. They could be taught for an hour a week without affecting other subjects.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Is it more important to be good at many things or excellent at one thing?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: 多くのことができるのと、一つのことに秀でるのと、どちらが大切ですか。
model: It depends on the job, but I think it is best to have one main strength and some general skills. That way you are valuable but also flexible.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Why do some people learn faster than others?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: なぜ学ぶのが速い人とそうでない人がいるのですか。
model: Motivation is a big factor. People who are really interested practise more. Good study habits and a supportive environment also make a difference.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: Should children be pushed to take many after-school lessons?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: 子どもにたくさんの習い事をさせるべきですか。
model: Not too many. Children need free time to play and rest. One or two activities they really enjoy are better than five they are forced to do.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2a.q: How has the internet changed the way people learn skills?
ielts_p3_2a.ja: インターネットは技能の学び方をどう変えましたか。
model: It has made learning much more accessible. You can watch a video tutorial on almost anything for free, although it is harder to get feedback than with a real teacher.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: What skills will people need for jobs in the future?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 将来の仕事にはどんなスキルが必要になりますか。
model: People will need to be flexible and keep learning, because technology changes so fast. Skills that machines cannot easily copy, such as creativity and teamwork, will be especially valuable.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Do older people find it harder to learn new technology?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 年配の人は新しい技術を学ぶのが難しいと思いますか。
model: Generally yes, because they did not grow up with it. But with patient teaching, many older people learn to use smartphones very well.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Is it important to keep learning throughout your life?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 一生学び続けることは大切ですか。
model: Definitely. Learning keeps your mind active, and in many jobs you have to update your knowledge regularly, just like pilots who train every year.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Should companies pay for their employees' training?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 会社は社員の研修費を払うべきですか。
model: I think they should, because the company benefits directly when its staff become more skilled. It also makes employees more loyal.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Which jobs are likely to disappear in the future?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 将来なくなりそうな仕事は何ですか。
model: Jobs that involve repeating the same task, such as some factory or data entry work, may be done by machines. However, new jobs will also appear.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Is a university degree still necessary to get a good job?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 良い仕事に就くのに大学の学位は今でも必要ですか。
model: For some careers, like medicine or engineering, definitely. In other fields, practical skills and experience are becoming just as important as a degree.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.q: Should older workers be encouraged to keep working?
ielts_p3_2b.ja: 高齢の労働者に働き続けるよう勧めるべきですか。
model: If they want to and are healthy, yes. They have a lot of experience to share, and many people enjoy feeling useful.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_2b.ja: 仕事の満足感は何から生まれますか。
model: Feeling that your work matters is the most important thing. Good colleagues and the chance to keep learning also make a big difference.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Who are the role models for young people today?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 今の若者のロールモデルはだれですか。
model: Many young people look up to athletes and pop stars, but I think teachers and family members are still important, because they are the people we see every day.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Do famous people have a responsibility to behave well?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 有名人には良いふるまいをする責任がありますか。
model: Yes, to some extent. Millions of young fans copy what they do, so if a celebrity behaves badly, it can send the wrong message.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Are parents the most important role models for children?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 親は子どもにとっていちばん大切なロールモデルですか。
model: In most cases, yes. Children learn habits and values by watching their parents, often without realising it.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: How do social media influencers affect young people?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: SNSのインフルエンサーは若者にどんな影響を与えますか。
model: They can be positive, for example by sharing study tips or healthy habits. However, some of them make young people compare themselves with unrealistic images.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Can a person be a role model without being famous?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 有名でなくてもロールモデルになれますか。
model: Of course. Teachers, coaches and older brothers or sisters influence young people every day, often more than celebrities.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: What qualities make someone a good leader?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 良いリーダーにはどんな資質がありますか。
model: A good leader listens to others, makes decisions calmly and takes responsibility when things go wrong.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Do people change their opinions because of others?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 人は他人の影響で意見を変えますか。
model: Yes, quite often, especially when they respect the other person. Social media also makes people more likely to follow the majority.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3a.q: Is it good for young people to copy their heroes?
ielts_p3_3a.ja: 若者がヒーローのまねをするのはよいことですか。
model: It can be, if they copy good habits like hard work. But they should also think for themselves and not copy everything blindly.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: How important are friends compared with family?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 友達は家族と比べてどのくらい大切ですか。
model: Both are important, but in different ways. Family support is usually more stable, while friends are the people we share our interests and problems with as we grow up.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: Do people spend less time with their families than in the past?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 昔より家族と過ごす時間は減っていますか。
model: I think so. Parents often work long hours, and children are busy with clubs and cram schools, so families rarely eat dinner together.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.ja: 良い友達とはどんな人ですか。
model: Someone you can trust and who is honest with you, even when the truth is not pleasant to hear.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: Is it easier to make friends now because of the Internet?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: インターネットのおかげで友達を作りやすくなりましたか。
model: It is easier to meet people with the same hobbies online, but I think it is harder to build deep friendships without meeting face to face.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: How do friendships change as people get older?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 年齢とともに友情はどう変わりますか。
model: People usually have fewer friends but closer ones. They also have less free time because of work and family, so they see their friends less often.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: Is it possible to be friends with someone you have never met in person?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 会ったことのない人と友達になれますか。
model: I think so. Many people make real friends through online games or study groups. Meeting in person later can make the friendship even stronger.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: Should parents choose their children's friends?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 親は子どもの友達を選ぶべきですか。
model: Not really. Parents can give advice, but children need to learn to judge people for themselves.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_3b.q: Why do some people prefer to spend time alone?
ielts_p3_3b.ja: 一人で過ごすのを好む人がいるのはなぜですか。
model: Some people recharge their energy by being alone. It gives them time to think, read or work on their hobbies without distractions.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: How has technology changed the way people communicate?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 技術によって人々のコミュニケーションはどう変わりましたか。
model: It has made communication instant and cheap. We can video call someone on the other side of the world, but some people now prefer messages to real conversations.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: Do people rely too much on their smartphones?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 人々はスマートフォンに頼りすぎていますか。
model: Many people do. For example, people use maps apps so often that they cannot find their way without them, and they check their phones even during meals.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: What problems can new technology cause for older people?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 新しい技術は高齢者にどんな問題を起こしますか。
model: Many services are moving online, such as banking and booking tickets, so older people who are not confident with technology can be left behind.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: Will robots do more household tasks in the future?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 将来、ロボットはもっと家事をするようになるでしょうか。
model: I think so. Robot vacuum cleaners are already common, and as prices fall, robots that can cook or fold laundry may become normal.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: Is technology making people less patient?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 技術のせいで人々は我慢強くなくなっていますか。
model: Probably. We are used to getting information and products instantly, so waiting even a few minutes can feel frustrating.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: Should there be age limits for using social media?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: SNSの利用に年齢制限を設けるべきですか。
model: Yes, I think so. Young children are not ready to deal with online pressure or strangers, so a minimum age protects them.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: What are the benefits of online banking and shopping?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: ネットバンキングやネット通販の利点は何ですか。
model: They save a lot of time, and you can do them at any time of day. They are especially helpful for people who live far from shops.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4a.q: Do you think people will still use cash in the future?
ielts_p3_4a.ja: 将来も人々は現金を使うと思いますか。
model: Less and less, but I do not think it will disappear completely. Some people prefer cash, and it is useful when there is a power cut.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: Should children use computers at school from a young age?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 子どもは小さいころから学校でコンピューターを使うべきですか。
model: Yes, but in moderation. Basic digital skills are essential, but young children also need to learn by writing by hand and playing with others.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: Can online lessons replace teachers in the classroom?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: オンライン授業は教室の先生の代わりになりますか。
model: Not completely. Online lessons are useful for explaining facts, but a teacher in the room can notice when a student is confused and motivate them.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: What are the risks of students using AI to do their homework?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 生徒がAIで宿題をすることの危険は何ですか。
model: The main risk is that students stop thinking for themselves. If AI writes their essays, they will not develop their own writing and reasoning skills.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: How might classrooms look different in twenty years?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 20年後の教室はどう違っているでしょうか。
model: Perhaps every student will have a personal learning programme on a device, and teachers will spend more time on discussions and projects than on lectures.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: Should mobile phones be banned in schools?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 学校でスマホを禁止すべきですか。
model: Not completely. They can be useful for research, but there should be clear rules, such as keeping them in bags during lessons.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: What skills do teachers need in the digital age?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: デジタル時代の教師にはどんな能力が必要ですか。
model: They need to use technology confidently, but more importantly, they need to teach students how to judge whether information online is reliable.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: Is it better to read books on paper or on a screen?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 紙の本と画面、どちらで読むほうがよいですか。
model: For studying, I think paper is better, because it is easier to concentrate and take notes. Screens are convenient for carrying many books when travelling.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_4b.q: How can schools make sure all students have access to technology?
ielts_p3_4b.ja: 学校はどうやって全生徒が技術を使えるようにできますか。
model: Schools can lend tablets to students who do not have one and provide free internet access in libraries.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: Why are parks important in cities?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 都市において公園はなぜ大切ですか。
model: Parks give people a place to relax and exercise for free. They also help to cool the city in summer and are good for wildlife.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: Should more money be spent on public spaces?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 公共の空間にもっとお金を使うべきですか。
model: I believe so. Good public spaces improve people's health and give communities a place to meet, which may reduce loneliness.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: Do children today spend less time outdoors than in the past?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 今の子どもは昔より外で過ごす時間が少ないですか。
model: Yes, I think they do. They have more indoor entertainment, such as games and videos, and parents may worry more about safety.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: What can be done to encourage people to go outside more?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 人々がもっと外に出るように、何ができますか。
model: Local governments could organise free events in parks, like outdoor concerts or exercise classes. Building safe walking and cycling paths would also help.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: Should cars be banned from city centres?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 都市の中心部から車を締め出すべきですか。
model: In some areas, yes. Car-free streets are safer and quieter, and they are good for shops because people walk more slowly and look around.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: What kinds of outdoor activities are popular in your country?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: あなたの国ではどんな屋外活動が人気ですか。
model: Hiking and camping are very popular, and in spring many people have picnics under the cherry trees.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: Do people need to live near nature to be happy?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 人は自然の近くに住まないと幸せになれませんか。
model: Not necessarily, but even a small park or some trees can make a big difference to how people feel.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5a.q: How has city life changed in recent years?
ielts_p3_5a.ja: 近年、都市の生活はどう変わりましたか。
model: Cities have become more crowded and expensive, but there are also more cafés, cycle lanes and green spaces than before.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5b.q: How can people protect the natural environment?
ielts_p3_5b.ja: 人々はどうやって自然環境を守ることができますか。
model: In daily life, people can reduce waste and use public transport. On a bigger scale, governments need to protect forests and coastlines from overdevelopment.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5b.q: Is it the responsibility of individuals or governments to protect nature?
ielts_p3_5b.ja: 自然を守るのは個人の責任ですか、それとも政府の責任ですか。
model: Both, but governments have more power. Individuals can change their habits, but only governments can make laws that affect whole industries.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5b.q: Why do some people prefer the countryside to the city?
ielts_p3_5b.ja: 都会より田舎を好む人がいるのはなぜですか。
model: Mainly for the peace and quiet. The air is cleaner, houses are cheaper, and people feel closer to nature.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5b.q: How will climate change affect the way people spend time outdoors?
ielts_p3_5b.ja: 気候変動は人々の屋外での過ごし方にどう影響しますか。
model: Summers are getting hotter, so people may avoid going out in the middle of the day. Outdoor sports and events might move to the early morning or evening.
points: 意見 → 理由 → 例
一般論として(people / society)

ielts_p3_5b.q: Should people be fined for dropping litter?
